reader.title: Rising Fawn marshal shooting
bases: The only account (A24, A25, A30) says a marshal shot dead a Black man he was about to arrest; no crowd or private party is mentioned.
Every report (A24, A25, A28, A30) is a copy or abridgment of one Decatur, Ala., special of Sept. 29; no independent local account was found.

summary.text: The Rising Fawn marshal shooting was the killing of an unnamed Black man by Marshal J. M. Surry at Rising Fawn on the morning of September 29, 1882.
According to the only account, a special telegraphed from Decatur, Alabama, the man tried to shoot the marshal as he was about to be arrested, and the marshal shot him dead.
The story reached papers across the West as a one-sentence wire item.
The dispatch, dated September 29 and relayed through New York, said that at Rising Fawn "this morning a desperate negro attempted to shoot Marshal J. M. Surry, who was about to arrest him."
It added only that "The Marshal shot the negro dead."
The man was not named, and the dispatch gave no reason for the attempted arrest, no witnesses and no source for the claim that he had tried to shoot first.
No report of an inquest, arrest or official inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage.
The Eureka Daily Sentinel in Nevada and the Salt Lake Daily Herald printed the special on September 30 among other telegraphic news, the Sentinel under the headline "Attempt to Shoot a Marshal."

The Weekly Phoenix Herald ran the same text on October 6 as "A Negro Shot Dead," while the Northern Pacific Farmer of Dakota reduced it on October 5 to a crime brief calling the man "a desperado negro."
Every version gave the marshal's account as fact and identified the dead man only by race.
The Northern Pacific Farmer's brief placed the shooting "At Decatur, Ala." and spelled the marshal's name Surrey, apparently folding the dispatch's dateline into the scene.
The fuller dispatch distinguished Decatur, where the news was sent from, and Rising Fawn, where the shooting took place, but did not say in which state Rising Fawn lay.

accounts.label: Decatur, Ala., special (wire report)
accounts.gist: At Rising Fawn on the morning of Sept. 29 a Black man attempted to shoot Marshal J. M. Surry, who was about to arrest him, and the marshal shot him dead. The dispatch names no witness and gives only this version.

accounts.label: Abridged crime brief
accounts.gist: Repeats the story without a date, placing it 'At Decatur, Ala.' and naming the marshal Surrey.

framing.detail: Papers in Nevada, Utah, Arizona and Dakota ran the dispatch verbatim or abridged among other telegraph items, under heads such as 'Attempt to Shoot a Marshal' and 'A Negro Shot Dead', presenting the marshal's account as fact.

conflicts.note: The brief appears to be an abridgment that collapsed the dateline into the scene; the fuller dispatch distinguishes the two and is the better evidence.
A spelling variant of the same name in the abridged brief.

record_check.dossier: Only the dispatch's dateline (Decatur, Ala.) is Alabama; no report gives the state of Rising Fawn. Georgia papers seen in the search place a Rising Fawn in Dade County, Ga. (see flags), so the state is uncertain.
Marshal J. M. Surry (Surrey in one brief).

record_check.dossier: Supported, but only as the dispatch's unsourced claim; the reason for the arrest is not reported.
